verdict.rationale: cubic offers several programmatic surfaces of its own, but nothing documents a general API that matches the UI. There is an Analytics API for PR-level data and an MCP server for reading findings, requesting reviews, triaging scan issues and managing subscriptions and seats. Repository config is also handled as code via cubic.yaml. The OpenAPI probe found no spec, and many UI features have no documented API equivalent: wiki, auto-approval settings, cross-repo linking, stack merging and the chat sidebar. Missing for 10: a general-purpose public REST API with parity to the UI, a published OpenAPI spec, API coverage of settings and workflows beyond analytics and MCP, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Analytics API gives you PR-level data on how many issues were flagged, how many were fixed, how much AI code was authored, etc.
Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, and triage PR or codebase scan issues.
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
